dedupe_keys.name: ai data centre flexibility in grid capacity expansion planning defer or shift

description: This paper builds a quantitative grid planning model that treats AI data centres as flexible, not rigid loads, to address the large-load interconnection bottleneck. It embeds the temporal and spatial shifting capabilities of data centres in a grid capacity expansion framework and evaluates their effects on additional generation, operational cost and network congestion. The numerical study finds that flexibility benefits are not felt uniformly and that more flexibility does not always mean less generation capacity; depending on data centre location, flexibility range and grid load conditions, flexible AI load can cut grid investment and operating costs by 3 to 21 percent, and longer deferral of AI compute has diminishing returns. Producer: Yize Chen and Xiaogui Zheng; the abstract page shows a first submission on 7 April 2026 (eight pages, five figures, in submission, systems and control). Coverage: a numerical study on a test grid, not a named real system. Access: free PDF and HTML on arXiv; no code or data repository was stated on the page. Licence and cost: free to read; licence CC-BY-4.0 (the paper, as linked on its arXiv abstract page). Caveats: an unreviewed preprint, and its results depend on the assumed flexibility ranges and test network. Simulation uses: the formulation can be reused for capacity planning and optimisation studies that couple data centre demand with generation and network expansion. Related record: the EPRI DCFlex flexible load tariffs and survey dataset (data-epri-dcflex-flexible-load-tariffs-and-survey).
